newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal, corn prices edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal, corn prices edge higher.

text.p: Thai soymeal and corn prices edged up from last week, traders said.

Local stocks of soymeal were falling, but supplies were expected to increase and prices should ease with the arrival next week of additional imported soymeal from India and almost four cargoes of U.S. soybeans bought by a major oil crusher.
The C Tausin is expected to arrive with 47,849 tonnes.
Thai Vegetable Oil was said to be the buyer.

Other major discharges included 37,085 tonnes of soymeal and 16,031 tonnes of soybeans from the U.S. The CSK Glory, which arrived on February 13, was chartered by Cargill with Charoen Phokpand as the buyer.
Soymeal prices were quoted around 9.55 baht a kg from 9.30-9.40 last week.
Traders said no corn had been imported so far as the industry was still waiting for the commerce ministry to come up with the new schedule for zero-tariff imports.
But buying had been active in the local market as major feed producers chased the price up in an attempt to persuade the government to allow imports soon.
"If the prices in Bangkok market reach 4.50 baht a kg ,which was earlier set as a benchmark by the government, it might be easier to ask them to open for imports," said one trader.
Corn was quoted at about 4.38-4.40, up from 4.30-4.35 last week.
